subject: english
text: In 'A Short Monsoon Diary', who is the writer of the diary entries?
explanation: 'A Short Monsoon Diary' is compiled from the personal diary entries of the well-known Indian writer Ruskin Bond.

options.text: Ruskin Bond
Satyajit Ray
Rabindranath Tagore
William Blake

subject: english
text: In the diary entry of June 25, how does the author describe Mussoorie after the rain has started?
explanation: The author describes the monsoon bringing lush green growth and hills covered in wild dahlias, turning the hill station into a beautiful sight.

options.text: As a hill station that looks like a paradise, with hills covered in wild dahlias.
As a town completely flooded with muddy water and blocked roads.
As a dry and dusty place waiting for the next monsoon shower.
As a crowded tourist hub filled with cars and people.

subject: english
text: In 'A Short Monsoon Diary', why does the writer mention the cobra lily?
explanation: The author notes that the cobra lily rearing its head shows the monsoon is here, and later when its seeds turn red, it signals that the rains are coming to an end.

options.text: Its appearance signals the start of the monsoon, and its seeds turning red signals the end of the monsoon.
It is a deadly poisonous flower that grows in the valleys.
The local people use its leaves to protect themselves from leeches.
It is the favorite flower of the leopards visiting Mussoorie.

subject: english
text: What is the name of the assistant device that helped Stephen Hawking communicate with his visitors in 'A Visit to Cambridge'?
explanation: Stephen Hawking communicated by tapping a switch in his hand, which sent signals to a computer voice synthesizer that spoke for him.

options.text: A computer voice synthesizer operated by a switch in his hand.
A personal nurse who read his lip movements.
A sign language translator from Cambridge University.
His daughter who spoke on his behalf.

subject: english
text: In 'A Visit to Cambridge', how did the author, Firdaus Kanga, feel after his meeting with Stephen Hawking?
explanation: Kanga felt deeply inspired and comforted, seeing Hawking as a symbol of immense mental strength despite his severe physical disability.

options.text: Inspired and stronger, realizing that physical limitations do not define the capabilities of the mind.
Depressed and sad about Hawking's physical condition.
Disappointed because Hawking did not speak much to him.
Jealous of Hawking's international fame and academic success.

subject: english
text: In the story 'Princess September', what happened to the little singing bird when the Princess put him in the cage?
explanation: The bird valued his freedom above all else; being caged made him miserable, so he stopped singing and eating.

options.text: He stopped singing and refused to eat, losing all his joy.
He sang even more beautifully because he felt safe.
He managed to bend the golden bars and escaped instantly.
He became friends with the eight green parrots.

subject: english
text: Why did Princess September's sisters advise her to put the little bird in a cage?
explanation: Out of jealousy, the eight sisters advised Princess September to lock the bird in a cage, claiming it was for the bird's own safety.

options.text: They were jealous of the bird's beautiful singing and wanted to make September unhappy.
They feared the bird would be eaten by the palace cats.
They wanted to borrow the bird to show to the King.
They thought the bird was planning to fly away forever.

subject: english
text: What pool did Ranji find in the forest in 'The Fight', and how was it different from the pools in the Rajputana desert?
explanation: The forest pool had clean, cold water coming from a spring, which was a sharp contrast to the muddy, dried-up pools Ranji was used to in the desert.

options.text: It had clean, cold, and translucent water that did not dry up, unlike the muddy, sticky pools of the desert.
It was a thermal hot spring surrounded by rocks.
It was a huge lake used by wild animals for drinking.
It was a dry, sandy bed where water accumulated only during rains.

subject: english
text: In 'The Fight', what did Suraj do when Ranji showed him how to dive and swim underwater?
explanation: Suraj was amazed by Ranji's swimming skills and proposed a deal: if Ranji taught him to dive, he would make sure no one troubled Ranji at the pool.

options.text: He was astonished and asked Ranji to teach him how to dive.
He got angry and accused Ranji of showing off.
He laughed at Ranji and claimed he could do it better.
He ran away to call his friends for help.

subject: english
text: In 'The Open Window', what was the tragedy that Vera described to Framton Nuttel?
explanation: Vera fabricated a tragic story that Mrs. Sappleton's husband and brothers drowned in a bog three years ago, and she kept the window open hoping they would return.

options.text: Her aunt's husband and brothers went out for shooting three years ago and never returned, having been engulfed in a bog.
The house was attacked by ghosts of former owners.
Her aunt lost her memory after a horse-riding accident.
The window was left open because the glass was broken during a storm.

subject: english
text: Why did Framton Nuttel run out of the house in a wild hurry at the end of 'The Open Window'?
explanation: Having believed Vera's ghost story, Framton was terrified when he saw the husband and brothers walk through the window, making him flee in horror.

options.text: He saw the three 'dead' figures returning through the open window and thought they were ghosts.
He had a sudden panic attack due to his illness.
He realized that Vera was playing a joke on him.
Mrs. Sappleton asked him to leave because he was boring.

subject: english
text: Fill in the blank with the correct modal verb to show permission: '_______ I borrow your pen for a moment, please?'
explanation: 'May' is the most formal and appropriate modal verb used to request permission.

options.text: May
Must
Should
Would

subject: english
text: Choose the correct synonym of the word 'Pensive'.
explanation: 'Pensive' means engaged in, involving, or reflecting deep or serious thought; 'thoughtful' is its closest synonym.

options.text: Thoughtful
Happy
Careless
Angry

subject: english
text: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: 'If he _______ faster, he would have won the race.'
explanation: In the third conditional (unreal past), the 'if'-clause uses the past perfect tense ('had run') while the main clause uses 'would have + past participle'.

options.text: had run
has run
ran
would run

subject: english
text: Choose the option that correctly changes this sentence into passive voice: 'The teacher is checking the notebooks.'
explanation: The active sentence is in the present continuous tense, so its passive form is 'am/is/are + being + past participle'. Since 'notebooks' is plural, 'are being checked' is used.

options.text: The notebooks are being checked by the teacher.
The notebooks were checked by the teacher.
The notebooks have been checked by the teacher.
The notebooks is being checked by the teacher.

subject: english
text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the word 'effect' as a noun.
explanation: 'Effect' is primarily used as a noun meaning result or consequence, whereas 'affect' is a verb meaning to influence.

options.text: The new rule will have a positive effect on the students.
The new rule will positive effect the students.
How does the weather effect your mood?
The medicine did not effect him at all.

subject: english
text: Complete the sentence with the correct conjunction: 'Although he is rich, _______ he is very down-to-earth.'
explanation: Clauses starting with 'Although' are classically paired with 'yet' (or just a comma), not 'but'.

options.text: yet
but
still
therefore

subject: english
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to grease someone's palm'?
explanation: The idiom 'to grease someone's palm' means to give someone money in order to persuade them to do something dishonest (to bribe).

options.text: To bribe someone
To help someone with manual labor
To praise someone falsely
To wash someone's hands

subject: english
text: Which of the following sentences has a misplaced modifier?
explanation: In 'Cluttered with papers, she cleaned the desk before leaving', 'Cluttered with papers' incorrectly modifies 'she', suggesting that the girl herself was cluttered with papers.

options.text: Cluttered with papers, the desk was cleaned by her before leaving.
Cluttered with papers, she cleaned the desk before leaving.
She cleaned the desk, which was cluttered with papers, before leaving.
Before leaving, she cleaned the desk that was cluttered with papers.

subject: english
text: Identify the sentence that is grammatically correct regarding the relative clause pronoun agreement:
explanation: In the structure 'It is [pronoun] who...', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the subject pronoun 'I', so the verb must agree with 'I' ('am').

options.text: It is I who am to blame for the mistake.
It is me who is to blame for the mistake.
It is I who is to blame for the mistake.
It is me who am to blame for the mistake.

subject: english
text: Which of the following sentences correctly uses a noun clause as a subject?
explanation: 'What he said' is a noun clause acting as the subject of the linking verb 'was'.

options.text: What he said was very inspiring to the entire class.
He said what was very inspiring to the entire class.
The class was inspired by what he said.
That he was very inspiring was believed by the class.

subject: english
text: Choose the sentence that is free from error regarding subject-verb agreement with parenthetical phrases:
explanation: Parenthetical phrases starting with 'along with' do not change the number of the subject. The subject remains singular ('The teacher'), taking a singular verb ('has').

options.text: The teacher, along with all her students, has attended the seminar.
The teacher, along with all her students, have attended the seminar.
The teacher, along with all her students, are attending the seminar.
The teacher along with all her students were attending the seminar.

subject: english
text: Identify the sentence that contains a gerund acting as the object of a preposition:
explanation: In 'She is fond of playing the violin', 'playing' is a gerund (noun form of verb) that acts as the object of the preposition 'of'.

options.text: She is fond of playing the violin.
Playing the violin is her favorite hobby.
She loves to play the violin in her free time.
The girl playing the violin is my sister.

subject: english
text: What is the grammatical function of the word 'where' in the sentence: 'He did not know where to go.'
explanation: 'Where' acts as a relative adverb introducing the infinitive phrase and indicating place.

options.text: Relative adverb
Relative pronoun
Coordinating conjunction
Interrogative pronoun

subject: english
text: Identify the correct word to fill in the blank: 'The new rules will _______ the entire school community.'
explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to make a difference to or influence, which fits the grammatical position of the sentence.

options.text: affect
effect
infect
defect
